course.title: Professional Development
course.description: Build the workplace behaviours, communication, teamwork, productivity and career skills that turn technical knowledge into sustained professional success. Beginner to confident professional.

modules.title: Module 1: Professional ethics and workplace behaviour

lessons.title: Lesson 1.1: Integrity and accountability
lessons.description: Do what you say; own outcomes.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Explain integrity and accountability with workplace examples and apply them to a realistic scenario.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.2: Professional conduct and etiquette
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

List practical behaviours that signal professionalism in meetings, messages and shared spaces.

lessons.title: Lesson 1.3: Handling workplace challenges
lessons.description: Conflict, pressure and ethical grey areas.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Use a simple framework to respond to conflict or ethical pressure without escalating harm.

lessons.title: Module 1 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 1 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: Accountability means:
Blaming others
*Owning your commitments and the results of your actions
Avoiding all responsibility
Only following orders blindly
explain: Ownership of outcomes.
level: 1

Q: Integrity at work is best shown by:
Hiding mistakes
*Aligning words and actions, even when inconvenient
Only when observed
Competing unfairly
explain: Consistency of character.
level: 1

Q: Professional etiquette includes:
Interrupting constantly
*Punctuality, respectful language and appropriate channels
Sharing private messages publicly
Ignoring deadlines
explain: Respect and reliability.
level: 1

Q: When you make a mistake the professional response is:
Cover it up
*Acknowledge, correct, and prevent recurrence
Blame the nearest colleague
Leave the job immediately
explain: Own and fix.
level: 1

Q: Ethical grey areas should be handled by:
Ignoring them
*Seeking guidance, applying organisational values, and documenting decisions when needed
Always choosing the easiest path
Publicly shaming others first
explain: Values + advice + transparency.
level: 2

Q: Reliability is demonstrated by:
Promising everything
*Delivering on commitments or communicating early when at risk
Only working when motivated
Avoiding hard tasks
explain: Follow-through.
level: 1

Q: Respectful disagreement means:
Never disagreeing
*Challenging ideas without attacking people
Raising your voice
Using sarcasm
explain: Ideas vs persons.
level: 2

Q: Confidential information should be:
Shared widely for transparency
*Protected according to policy and need-to-know
Posted on social media
Ignored
explain: Confidentiality is a duty.
level: 1

Q: A simple conflict approach is:
Win at all costs
*Listen, state impact, propose options, agree next steps
Avoid all discussion
Escalate immediately every time
explain: Structured resolution.
level: 2

Q: Professional behaviour ultimately supports:
Only personal branding
*Trust, teamwork and organisational effectiveness
Avoiding all growth
Competition only
explain: Trust enables results.
level: 1

lessons.title: Lesson 2.1: Clear written communication
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Write short workplace messages with a clear purpose, needed context and requested action.

lessons.title: Lesson 2.2: Speaking and presenting
lessons.description: Structure and delivery for small audiences.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Structure a short verbal update: purpose, key points, ask.

lessons.title: Lesson 2.3: Active listening and feedback
lessons.description: Understand before responding; give useful feedback.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Practise listening to understand and giving specific, constructive feedback.

lessons.title: Module 2 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 2 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: A clear workplace message should state:
Only jokes
*Purpose, needed context and the requested action
Every possible detail first
Nothing about next steps
explain: Purpose + context + ask.
level: 1

Q: Active listening prioritises:
Planning your reply while the other person talks
*Understanding the speaker before responding
Interrupting to correct
Checking your phone
explain: Understand first.
level: 1

Q: Constructive feedback is:
Vague and personal
*Specific, about behaviour or work product, and aimed at improvement
Only negative
Public shaming
explain: Specific + improvable.
level: 1

Q: A short verbal update works well with:
No structure
*Purpose, 2–4 key points, and a clear ask or conclusion
Reading a long document aloud
Only slides with tiny text
explain: Structure aids retention.
level: 2

Q: Subject lines in email should:
Be empty
*Summarise the topic or action needed
Contain only emojis
Be as long as the body
explain: Scannable subject lines help.
level: 1

Q: When receiving feedback you should:
Defend immediately always
*Listen fully, clarify, and decide what to apply
Ignore it
Argue about tone only
explain: Learning posture.
level: 2

Q: Adapting communication to the audience means:
Using the same jargon for everyone
*Adjusting detail and language to what the listener needs
Avoiding all technical terms forever
Only writing
explain: Audience fit.
level: 1

Q: A request is clearer when it includes:
No deadline
*What is needed, by when, and any constraints
Only “ASAP”
Multiple unrelated asks buried in paragraphs
explain: Clarity enables action.
level: 1

Q: Summarising what you heard before responding:
Wastes time
*Confirms understanding and reduces miscommunication
Is only for therapy
Shows weakness
explain: Confirmation prevents errors.
level: 2

Q: The goal of professional communication is:
Impressing with complexity
*Shared understanding and effective action
Winning arguments only
Avoiding all writing
explain: Understanding + action.
level: 1

lessons.title: Lesson 3.1: Effective teamwork
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Describe behaviours that make teams more effective and apply them in a small-group scenario.

lessons.title: Lesson 3.2: Decision-making and responsibility
lessons.description: How groups decide and who owns outcomes.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Distinguish consultation from decision rights and clarify ownership of follow-through.

lessons.title: Lesson 3.3: Working across differences
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Use practical habits that turn diverse viewpoints into better solutions rather than conflict.

lessons.title: Module 3 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 3 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: Effective teams usually have:
No shared goals
*Clear goals, roles and norms for how they work together
Only one person doing everything
Constant unexplained changes
explain: Clarity enables coordination.
level: 1

Q: Decision rights should be:
Ambiguous so everyone is equal
*Clear so people know who decides after input
Always unanimous
Hidden
explain: Clarity prevents deadlock.
level: 1

Q: Diverse perspectives help when:
They are ignored
*They are actively sought and integrated into better solutions
Only one view is allowed
Conflict is maximised for its own sake
explain: Inclusion improves outcomes.
level: 1

Q: Following through on team commitments builds:
Distrust
*Reliability and trust
Only individual glory
Avoidance of work
explain: Follow-through is social capital.
level: 1

Q: When roles are unclear teams often experience:
Perfect efficiency
*Duplication, gaps and friction
Automatic success
No need for communication
explain: Ambiguity costs.
level: 2

Q: Consultation means:
Everyone decides equally always
*Gathering input before a decision is made by the accountable person or process
Ignoring experts
Voting on every detail
explain: Input ≠ final decision right.
level: 2

Q: A practical inclusion habit is:
Interrupting quieter members
*Inviting contributions from quieter members and building on ideas
Only listening to seniority
Avoiding all disagreement
explain: Structured inclusion.
level: 1

Q: Shared norms might cover:
Nothing practical
*How the team communicates, meets, and handles deadlines
Only social events
Only individual goals
explain: Working agreements.
level: 2

Q: Owning a workstream means:
Doing nothing
*Being accountable for progress and raising risks early
Hiding problems
Blaming the team
explain: Ownership + transparency.
level: 1

Q: The point of collaboration is:
Meetings for their own sake
*Better results than individuals would achieve alone
Avoiding all individual work
Maximising email volume
explain: Results over process theatre.
level: 1

lessons.title: Lesson 4.1: Planning and prioritising
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Use a simple prioritisation method to plan a week of work.

lessons.title: Lesson 4.2: Managing time and focus
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Design a daily routine that protects blocks of focused time.

lessons.title: Lesson 4.3: Working effectively with tools
lessons.description: Calendars, task lists and communication hygiene.
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Set up a lightweight personal system for tasks and calendar that you will actually use.

lessons.title: Module 4 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 4 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: Urgent tasks are:
Always the most important
*Time-sensitive; they may or may not be important
Never important
The same as goals
explain: Urgency ≠ importance.
level: 1

Q: Protecting focus time means:
Being available for every interruption
*Scheduling and defending blocks for deep work
Only working at night
Avoiding all meetings forever
explain: Intentional focus blocks.
level: 1

Q: A usable task system is:
Perfectly complex
*Simple enough that you maintain it daily
Only in your head
Shared with everyone automatically
explain: Simplicity aids consistency.
level: 1

Q: Prioritisation should consider:
Only who shouts loudest
*Impact, deadlines, dependencies and goals
Only ease
Only novelty
explain: Multiple factors.
level: 2

Q: Communication hygiene includes:
CC’ing everyone on everything
*Using the right channel and reducing unnecessary noise
Never responding
Only using phone calls
explain: Right channel, less noise.
level: 2

Q: Batching similar tasks can:
Increase context switching
*Reduce context switching and improve efficiency
Eliminate all planning
Only work for email
explain: Batching reduces switching costs.
level: 2

Q: A weekly planning habit helps:
Only large corporations
*Align daily work with longer-term priorities
Avoid all flexibility
Replace all tools
explain: Weekly horizon connects to goals.
level: 1

Q: Saying no (or not now) to low-value requests:
Is unprofessional always
*Protects capacity for high-value work when done respectfully
Means you are lazy
Should be avoided forever
explain: Capacity is finite.
level: 2

Q: Calendar blocks for deep work should be:
Secret and frequently cancelled
*Treated as real commitments
Only aspirational
Filled with meetings
explain: Treat focus as a commitment.
level: 1

Q: Productivity systems fail most often when:
They are too simple
*They are too complex to maintain or disconnected from real priorities
They include a calendar
They include a task list
explain: Sustainability and relevance matter.
level: 1

modules.title: Module 5: Career development
modules.description: Goals, applications, interviews and continuous learning.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.1: Setting career goals
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Write a 12-month career goal and the three skills that would most advance it.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.2: CVs, applications and interviews
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Rewrite one experience bullet to emphasise impact and prepare for a common interview question.

lessons.title: Lesson 5.3: Networking and lifelong learning
lessons.notesHtml:
Aim

Identify two practical ways to learn in the next quarter and one relationship to strengthen professionally.

lessons.title: Module 5 review and assessment
lessons.notesHtml:
Module 5 review and assessment

10 questions. Pass mark 70 %.
lessons.quiz:
Q: A useful career goal is:
Vague and distant
*Specific enough to guide near-term skill and experience choices
Only about salary
Secret from mentors
explain: Specificity guides action.
level: 1

Q: Strong CV bullets emphasise:
Only duties
*Actions and measurable or observable impact
Only job titles
Personal hobbies only
explain: Impact over duty lists.
level: 1

Q: Interview answers are stronger when they:
Stay abstract
*Use concrete examples (situation, action, result)
Avoid all numbers
Criticise former colleagues
explain: STAR-style evidence.
level: 1

Q: Networking is best approached as:
Transactional asking only
*Building genuine professional relationships over time
Collecting business cards only
Avoiding all events
explain: Relationships compound.
level: 2

Q: Lifelong learning in a fast-changing field is:
Optional
*Essential for sustained relevance
Only for juniors
Replaced by AI completely
explain: Skills decay without practice.
level: 1

Q: Choosing which skills to build next should consider:
Only what is trendy on social media
*Your goals, market demand and comparative advantage
Only what is easiest
Only what your friends choose
explain: Goal + market + fit.
level: 2

Q: A portfolio or work samples help when:
You have nothing to show
*They provide concrete evidence of capability
They replace all conversation
They are password-free sensitive data
explain: Evidence beats claims.
level: 2

Q: Asking for informational advice from practitioners:
Is always an imposition
*Can be valuable when respectful, specific and grateful
Requires payment always
Should only be done once ever
explain: Thoughtful asks work.
level: 2

Q: Reflecting on projects after completion helps:
Only dwell on failure
*Extract lessons that improve future performance
Avoid all documentation
Replace planning
explain: Reflection fuels growth.
level: 1

Q: Career development is ultimately:
A one-time decision at age 20
*An ongoing process of goals, skills, relationships and contribution
Only the employer’s job
Avoidable if you work hard once
explain: Continuous process.
level: 1
